---
title: "03 · Nearest neighbors and plurality stability"
description: "Understand the fixed-candidate common-argmin law."
---

Pairwise agreements share a query and are dependent, so multiplying or adding
pairwise probabilities is wrong. In the fixed-candidate limit, the original and
projected score vectors become correlated Gaussian vectors. Their common-argmin
probability is the plurality kernel `p_q(rho)`.

```python
import numpy as np
from rpgeom.laws import plurality_kernel
rho = np.sqrt(20 / 10_000)
print(plurality_kernel(rho, q=8), "versus chance", 1/8)
```

The candidate count `q` is fixed in this theorem. Growing databases and hub
identity require different asymptotics; the project labels that boundary rather
than silently extrapolating.
